memories.memory_text: I remarked that the elevator was a very small room, and Wilson laughed as if I had said something funny.

grounded_facts: Chance is wheeled into Rand's hospital room for an X-ray, marking the beginning of their interaction.
memories.memory_text: I was wheeled into Rand's hospital room by Wilson, and I noticed Rand lifting his head as I came in.

grounded_facts: Medical procedure where Chance undergoes an X-ray in Rand's hospital room with technician Billings assisting.
memories.memory_text: I was helped onto the X-ray table by Wilson and the technician Billings, and I remember looking at Billings and noticing he was Black.

grounded_facts: Chance questions Billings about knowing Raphael after noticing his race, referencing a message from a Black man.
memories.memory_text: I saw that Billings was Black and wondered if he knew Raphael, so I asked him. When he said he didn't, I mentioned I had a message for Raphael from a Black man.

grounded_facts: Rand informs Chance about his medical condition, revealing his vulnerability and philosophical outlook on illness and wealth.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Mr. Rand that he has aplastic anemia, and I remember him saying it clearly to me.

grounded_facts: Rand expresses his view that it is better to be wealthy and sick than poor and sick, sharing his attitude toward illness and privilege.
memories.memory_text: I heard Mr. Rand say that he would rather be wealthy and sick than poor and sick, and I remember thinking about how he looked very unwell but surrounded by machines.

grounded_facts: Evening period in the hospital ward involving patient care, transfusions, and social exchanges.
memories.memory_text: I sensed it was evening because the nurses were busy with patient care, and I noticed Rand laying his head back after his transfusion.

grounded_facts: Rand invites Chance to join him for dinner, signaling a social connection between the two patients.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Rand that I would join them for dinner, and he asked me directly if I would come.

grounded_facts: Both men, lying flat, express hunger and agree to have dinner together, forming a moment of human connection.
memories.memory_text: I remember lying there and saying I was very hungry, and then Rand said he was too, and we agreed to have dinner together.

grounded_facts: Chance discloses that his business was shut down and locked by attorneys after the death of 'the Old Man' and Louise leaving.
memories.memory_text: I told Ben that my house and business were shut down and locked by the attorneys after the Old Man died and Louise left.

grounded_facts: Eve expresses sympathy for Chance's losses and offers assistance with the estate's facilities.
memories.memory_text: I was told that I could use their facilities if I needed to, and she expressed sympathy about my losses and asked if I wanted anyone notified.

grounded_facts: Rand shifts from formal address to proposing a first-name basis, signaling growing rapport.
memories.memory_text: Ben smiled and asked if he could call me Chauncey, and I said yes, then he told me to call him Ben.

grounded_facts: Allenby smiles and invites Chance to call him Robert, furthering social integration.
memories.memory_text: Robert smiled at me and invited me to call him by his first name, so I agreed and said I would call him Robert.

grounded_facts: Chance inquires about the presence of a garden and expresses his wish to work in it, indicating a shift in his intended role or purpose.
memories.memory_text: I asked if this house has a garden, and I told the man I would like to work in it.

grounded_facts: Rand enthusiastically affirms Chance's identification as a gardener, elevating it to a metaphor for productive capitalism.
memories.memory_text: I remember Rand saying that a businessman is like a gardener, making soil productive with his own hands and sweat, and creating value for family and community—he called it a brilliant metaphor, and I smiled at him when he laughed.

grounded_facts: Rand reacts strongly against Chance's metaphorical reference to the 'room upstairs', interpreting it as surrender, and urges him to fight back.
memories.memory_text: I told Ben Rand that all that's left for me is the room upstairs, and he reacted strongly, telling me not to give up and to fight back, but I just smiled and said it's a very pleasant room.

grounded_facts: A formal dinner gathering at Rand's estate with guests including Allenby, Eve, and Chance, where conversation turns to business, regulation, and personal circumstances.
memories.memory_text: I was at a formal dinner at Ben's estate with guests, where I spoke about my garden and how my house had been closed, and I remember the pauses and looks between us.

grounded_facts: Rand offers Chance a cigar from his humidor, initiating a gesture of camaraderie and testing.
memories.memory_text: I saw Mr. Rand offer me a cigar from his humidor, and I accepted it, saying I didn't know everything about him.

grounded_facts: Rand probes Chance's knowledge of him, framing honesty as rare and valuable.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Mr. Rand that no man knows everything about another, but he valued that I was honest enough to admit I don't know everything about him.

grounded_facts: A nighttime meeting in Rand's pool room where Rand engages Chance in conversation about ideology and potential collaboration.
memories.memory_text: I remember being in Mr. Rand's pool room at night, where he spoke while shooting pool, and I tried to light the cigar as he talked to me.

grounded_facts: Rand reveals his intention to start a financial assistance program for struggling American businessmen, framing it as a defense of middle-class values.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Rand that he wanted to start a financial assistance program to help American businessmen who were struggling with inflation and taxes, and that he saw this as defending middle-class values.

grounded_facts: Chance explicitly states he has no thoughts on the proposed financial program.
memories.memory_text: I told Ben no when he asked for my thoughts on the program because my leg was hurting and I couldn't think about it.

grounded_facts: Allenby declares it time for his patients to prepare for bed, asserting medical authority over both Chance and Rand.
memories.memory_text: I remember Allenby saying it was time for his patients to prepare for bed, and I knew he meant me and Ben.

grounded_facts: Rand positions businessmen as 'Gardeners' defending freedom against 'pollutants', attempting to align Chance with his worldview.
memories.memory_text: I heard Rand say that businessmen are 'Gardeners' who defend freedom against 'pollutants', and he tried to include me in that idea, but I didn't respond because my leg was sore and I didn't know what to say.

grounded_facts: Allenby physically removes Rand's cigar and ends the meeting, asserting control over Rand's behavior under medical pretense.
memories.memory_text: I saw Allenby take Ben's cigar and put it out, and then he ended the meeting.

grounded_facts: Wilson breaks into laughter upon making eye contact with Chance in the elevator, apologizing afterward but indicating he anticipated one of Chance's jokes.
memories.memory_text: I saw Wilson start laughing when he made eye contact with me in the elevator, and he apologized but seemed to expect I would say something funny.

grounded_facts: Wilson laughs and claims he expected Chance to make a joke about the elevator, preemptively attributing humor to Chance despite no such statement being made.
memories.memory_text: Wilson told me he thought I was going to make one of my jokes about the elevator, even though I didn't say anything.

grounded_facts: Eve tells Chance she feels dreadful about the accident but is genuinely pleased he is staying, highlighting her emotional dependence on his presence.
memories.memory_text: I remember Eve telling me how dreadful she felt about the accident but that she was genuinely pleased I was staying, which made me aware of how much she values my presence.

grounded_facts: Chance directly asks Eve if she plans to leave and close the house when Ben dies, marking a shift in tone and introducing a stark awareness of mortality.
memories.memory_text: I asked Eve if she planned to leave and close the house when Ben dies, and I could feel the tone change right away.

grounded_facts: After asking a disturbing question about Ben's death, Chance smiles at Eve, offering subtle comfort and easing the tension before she retreats.
memories.memory_text: After I asked her about Ben, I smiled at Eve to offer some comfort, and she stepped back into her room after a moment of silence.

grounded_facts: A brief encounter between Chance, Eve, and Wilson in the hallway after Chance is brought from the elevator.
memories.memory_text: I recall Wilson wheeling me out of the elevator and stopping when Eve came out of her bedroom; he stood stiffly as we spoke, and then after our talk, Eve closed her door and Wilson wheeled me down the hallway toward the guest room.

grounded_facts: Allenby examines Chance's injured leg, assessing recovery progress.
memories.memory_text: I walked outside with a limp, and Robert Allenby examined my leg, asking if I felt pain; I told him yes, but not badly, and he noted the swelling had gone down considerably.

grounded_facts: Annual meeting of Benjamin Rand's Financial Institute, from which he is excused due to health.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Benjamin Rand was supposed to speak at the annual meeting of his Financial Institute, but couldn't due to his health, and that the President would be coming here instead.

grounded_facts: Allenby reveals that the President will attend the Financial Institute meeting in place of Benjamin Rand.
memories.memory_text: I was told that the President would sit in for Benjamin Rand at the Financial Institute meeting, and I confirmed to Robert that I knew about it.

grounded_facts: Chance is scheduled to meet the President in Benjamin Rand's room at ten o'clock.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Ben to meet the President in his room at ten o'clock, and I remember confirming that I was to be there at that time.

grounded_facts: Chance becomes aware that he is expected to meet the President at ten o'clock, gaining time-sensitive knowledge.
memories.memory_text: I learned from Ben that I need to meet the President, and he told me to be in his room at ten o'clock.

grounded_facts: Chance reveals he already knows about the President's visit, surprising Allenby.
memories.memory_text: I remember when Allenby mentioned the President's visit, I told him yes, because Ben had already called me and said to be in his room at ten o'clock to meet the President.

grounded_facts: Chance chooses to walk instead of using the wheelchair, indicating improved mobility and desire for independence.
memories.memory_text: I decided to walk out to meet the President instead of staying in the wheelchair, even though I still have a limp, because I wanted to do it on my own.

grounded_facts: Smythe notices Chance appears confused and asks if he can help.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Smythe saw that I was confused and he asked if he could help me.

memories.memory_text: I remember Smythe asking me if I wished to see someone at the hospital.

grounded_facts: Chance expresses his desire to go to Rand Memorial Hospital, indicating a specific intention to visit someone there.
memories.memory_text: I told Smythe that I would like to go to Rand Memorial Hospital because I want to see Ben.

memories.memory_text: I followed Smythe down the hall after he understood what I needed.

grounded_facts: Rand readies himself in his hospital room for an upcoming meeting with the President.
memories.memory_text: I saw Rand sitting in his chair, all dressed up and ready for his meeting with the President when I came into the room.

grounded_facts: Rand has nurse Teresa apply makeup to appear healthier for his meeting with the President, masking his illness.
memories.memory_text: Rand told me that the nurse applied makeup to make him look healthier for the President, so he wouldn't think he was going to die during their talk.

grounded_facts: Rand expresses admiration for Chance's emotional stability, contrasting it with general human fear of death.
Rand tells Chance he admires his emotional balance and peaceful nature, unlike most people who fear death.
memories.memory_text: I remember Rand telling me he admired my emotional balance and peaceful nature, saying most people are filled with fear of death, but I don't stagger between fear and hope like they do.

grounded_facts: Chance observes and compliments the nurse's work on Rand's appearance, affirming the success of the grooming effort.
memories.memory_text: I told Rand that the nurse did a very good job on his appearance, because I could see it made him look much better.

grounded_facts: Chance gives a brief, distracted response while changing TV channels, showing limited engagement with Rand's serious reflection.
memories.memory_text: I said 'I see, Ben' while I was changing the channel, not fully focused on what he was saying.

grounded_facts: Rand shares his past thoughts about public office and explains how he chose to exert influence as a private citizen, emphasizing ethical responsibility and staying connected to the people.
memories.memory_text: I remember Ben telling me about how he once thought about public office but decided he could do more as a private citizen, using his wealth carefully and staying connected to the people.

grounded_facts: A formal meeting between Rand and the President, arranged to take place in the library.
memories.memory_text: I was told there would be a formal meeting with the President in the library.

grounded_facts: Rand refuses to use his wheelchair and decides to walk to meet the President despite his weakness, symbolizing his assertion of strength and dignity.
memories.memory_text: I saw Rand refuse his wheelchair and insist on walking to meet the President, as if to show he was still strong and in control.

grounded_facts: Rand puts his arm around Chance to support himself while walking, indicating trust and dependence.
memories.memory_text: I felt Rand put his arm around me to support himself as we walked, and he said, 'Shall we go, Chauncey?' like we were in this together.

grounded_facts: Rand comments positively on Mrs. Aubrey's efficiency, signaling trust and satisfaction.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Rand comment on Mrs. Aubrey's efficiency, seeing his trust and satisfaction in how she performed her duties.

grounded_facts: Rand tells Chance that Mrs. Aubrey is a good woman, sharing his positive assessment.
memories.memory_text: Rand told me that Mrs. Aubrey is a good woman, sharing his positive opinion with me directly.

grounded_facts: Chance agrees with Rand's positive assessment of Mrs. Aubrey upon first seeing her.
memories.memory_text: I agreed with Ben's assessment of Mrs. Aubrey, letting him know I shared his positive view.

grounded_facts: Woltz uses a metal detector to scan Rand and Chance before they enter the library, indicating heightened security protocols.
memories.memory_text: I saw Woltz take out a metal detector as Rand and I approached the library, preparing to screen us before we could enter.

grounded_facts: Woltz greets Rand politely with a verbal exchange upon his arrival.
memories.memory_text: I heard Woltz greet Mr. Rand politely with a 'Good morning,' and Mr. Rand asked how he was, and Woltz replied he was just fine, thank you.

grounded_facts: Woltz identifies and addresses Chance for the first time, initiating contact under formal circumstances.
memories.memory_text: Woltz turned to me and said, 'And you must be Mr. Gardiner,' and I answered yes, being addressed by my name for the first time in that formal setting.

grounded_facts: The President arrives at the library to visit Rand, expressing personal warmth and concern for his condition.
The President approaches Rand with both hands outstretched, calls him by name, and expresses personal affection.
memories.memory_text: I saw the President arrive in the library and go straight to Rand with both hands outstretched; he said it was good to see him and that he'd missed him, showing real warmth and concern.

grounded_facts: Chance initiates a two-handed handshake with the President, mirroring the President's earlier gesture to Rand.
memories.memory_text: I reached out with both hands to shake the President's hand, just as he had done with Rand a moment earlier.

grounded_facts: Rand formally introduces Chance as his house guest and dear friend to the President.
memories.memory_text: I heard Rand introduce me to the President as his dear friend and house guest.

grounded_facts: The President responds with mild surprise and amusement to Chance's observation about his television height.
memories.memory_text: I told the President he looked much taller on television, and I saw him pause and then laugh, as if amused by what I said.

grounded_facts: A private meeting in the library between Rand, the President, and Chance, ostensibly to discuss the President's upcoming speech.
memories.memory_text: I was present for a private meeting in the library where the President sat with Rand to discuss his upcoming speech, and I heard them talk about how dangerous temporary measures could be and how a straightforward speech might cause chaos.

grounded_facts: Rand evaluates the President's speech as generally good but warns against temporary measures, highlighting political risk.
memories.memory_text: I listened to Rand speak and remember him saying the President's speech could cause chaos, though he thought it was generally good.

grounded_facts: Chance responds to the mention of 'chance' in conversation as if being addressed directly, revealing his literal understanding.
memories.memory_text: I heard someone say 'chance' and thought they were talking to me, so I said 'Yes?' both times, just like before.

grounded_facts: The President gives Chance a quizzical look after he interrupts twice when his name is mentioned.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the President looked at me quizzically after I spoke up, as if he didn't expect me to respond when my name was mentioned.

grounded_facts: Chance uses a garden metaphor to suggest that economic cycles are natural and temporary, which Rand interprets as acceptance of inevitable economic seasons.
memories.memory_text: I spoke about how in my garden, there are seasons—spring and summer, but also fall and winter—and I said that as long as the roots are not severed, all is well and all will be well, because growth will return in time.

grounded_facts: Rand informs the President that the free enterprise system has reached a breaking point, warning of an imminent economic crash.
memories.memory_text: I heard Rand tell the President that the free enterprise system had reached its breaking point and that we were on the brink of an economic crash, and I recall him later saying we resist economic seasons just as we welcome nature's.

grounded_facts: The President praises Chance's statement as refreshing and optimistic, expressing envy for his 'solid sense'.
memories.memory_text: I remember the President telling me that my words were one of the most refreshing and optimistic things he'd heard in a long time, and he said he envied my good, solid sense.

grounded_facts: The President invites Chance to visit him and his family, indicating newfound respect and personal admiration.
memories.memory_text: The President told me I would honor him and his family with a visit, and I told him yes, I will.

grounded_facts: Rand thanks the President for visiting, calling it a privilege despite being a 'dying man'.
memories.memory_text: I saw Rand thank the President for visiting, calling it a privilege despite being a dying man.

grounded_facts: The President shakes Chance's hand upon arrival and again when departing, signaling respect and goodwill.
memories.memory_text: I shook the President's hand when he arrived and again when he was leaving, and I felt he showed me respect.

grounded_facts: A private meeting between the President, Rand, and Chance in the library during the morning.
memories.memory_text: I was in the library with the President and Rand that morning, and I remember smiling as the President paced and worried; he even asked me directly what I thought, then shook my hand before leaving.

grounded_facts: The President ends the meeting and departs the library.
memories.memory_text: I saw the President put out his cigarette and rise, then he left the library and I sat back down.

grounded_facts: Rand tells Chance he appreciates his straightforwardness and feels he can speak frankly with him.
memories.memory_text: I remember Rand telling me that he appreciates how direct I am and that he feels he can speak frankly with me.

grounded_facts: Rand suggests that Chance take charge of a financial assistance program and plans for him to meet with the Board.
memories.memory_text: I recall Rand suggesting that I should take charge of the financial assistance program and that he wants me to meet with the Board about it.

grounded_facts: Rand ends the conversation, citing sudden tiredness, and is assisted into his hospital room by Wilson and Perkins.
memories.memory_text: I was with Rand when he suddenly said he was very tired and needed to excuse himself, and then Wilson and Perkins helped him into his hospital room.

grounded_facts: As Rand enters his room, Chance expresses sorrow for his poor health.
memories.memory_text: As they took Rand into his room, I told him I was sorry that he was so sick, because I truly felt sorrow for him.

grounded_facts: Eve asks Chance about his relationship with the Old Man, seeking clarification on their connection.
memories.memory_text: Eve asked me if the Old Man was a relative or an intimate friend, wondering about our connection.

grounded_facts: Chance and Eve walk together in the garden, engaging in personal conversation about the Old Man and Louise.
memories.memory_text: I walked in the garden with Eve, and we talked about the Old Man and Louise; I told her he was a very wealthy man who looked after me since I was young, and she asked if I was close to Louise too.

grounded_facts: Eve asks whether Chance was romantically involved with Louise, revealing her personal concern or interest in his emotional availability.
memories.memory_text: I was told Eve thought Louise might have been someone I was romantically involved with, but she was only the maid.

grounded_facts: Eve subtly shifts position to stand nearer to Chance, indicating increasing emotional or romantic interest.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Eve moved a little closer to me as we walked, but I was more interested in the greenhouse and moved nearer to it.

grounded_facts: Chance physically moves closer to the greenhouse, showing growing interest in it.
Chance shows fascination and pleasure toward the greenhouse, indicating a shift in emotional focus and interest.
memories.memory_text: I moved closer to the greenhouse because I was fascinated by it, and when I saw it, I asked what it was and said I liked it very much.

grounded_facts: A group gathers in Rand's bedroom to watch the President's televised address to the Financial Institute.
memories.memory_text: I was in Rand's bedroom with Eve, Allenby, and the nurses, and we all watched the President's address on TV together.

grounded_facts: The President cites Rand and Chance in his address, quoting Chance's gardening metaphor as economic insight.
memories.memory_text: I heard the President mention Rand and me during his speech, and he quoted my words about the roots of industry being firmly planted and the economic prospects being sunny, just like I said.

grounded_facts: Rand experiences a sudden worsening of his condition, leading to heavy coughing and difficulty breathing, prompting medical intervention.
memories.memory_text: I saw Rand start coughing heavily and struggling to breathe, and I watched Allenby and the nurses rush to help him.

grounded_facts: Allenby uses a gesture to request Eve and Chance exit the room during Rand's medical episode.
Allenby signals for Eve and Chance to exit the bedroom to allow medical care for Rand without interference.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Allenby giving Eve and me a quick look before he motioned for us to leave the room so he could care for Rand without us in the way.

grounded_facts: Chance is informed of an incoming phone call from Sidney Courtney, the financial editor of the Washington Post, and agrees to take it.
memories.memory_text: I was told there was a phone call for me from Sidney Courtney, the financial editor of the Washington Post, and I agreed to take it.

grounded_facts: Eve tells Chance she is grateful for his presence with her and Ben during a difficult time.
memories.memory_text: I remember Eve telling me she was grateful for my presence with her and Ben during a difficult time.

grounded_facts: Chance rises and follows Mrs. Aubrey into the house after being called for a phone conversation.
memories.memory_text: I rose and followed Mrs. Aubrey into the house to take the phone call.

grounded_facts: Sid Courtney, a journalist from the Washington Post, attempts to conduct a phone interview with Chance Gardiner regarding a meeting involving the President and Mr. Rand.
memories.memory_text: I was told by a journalist named Sid Courtney from the Washington Post that he wanted to ask me about the meeting with the President and Mr. Rand.

grounded_facts: Courtney presses Chance for factual information about his professional role and affiliation with the First American Financial Corporation, which Chance declines to provide.
memories.memory_text: I was told that the journalist wanted to know about my relationship with the First American Financial Corporation and what my business is, but I chose not to provide that information.

grounded_facts: Chance refuses to answer further questions and abruptly hangs up the phone during an interview request from a Washington Post journalist.
memories.memory_text: I told the journalist I had nothing more to say and I hung up the phone, then went back to watching the TVs.

grounded_facts: Chance notices the service elevator and gets into it.
memories.memory_text: I came out of Mrs. Aubrey's office and noticed the service elevator, so I got in.

grounded_facts: Chance selects a floor by pressing a button in the elevator, initiating movement.
memories.memory_text: I looked at the buttons in the elevator and pressed one, feeling it move as I smiled.

grounded_facts: Jennifer expresses surprise and greets Chance upon seeing him in the basement, asking if he is looking for someone.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jennifer waiting with paperwork, and when I smiled at her, she greeted me as Mr. Gardiner and asked if I was looking for someone.

grounded_facts: Chance exits the elevator in the basement instead of the expected third floor, indicating a navigational error or system malfunction.
memories.memory_text: I stepped out of the elevator expecting to be on the third floor, but I found myself in the basement and felt puzzled by where I was.

memories.memory_text: I was told that the producer of 'This Evening' wanted me to be on the show as a replacement for the Vice President, who had canceled, and I accepted the invitation.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Aubrey delivers the news that Chance has been invited to appear on 'This Evening'.
memories.memory_text: I remember Mrs. Aubrey coming in and telling me that I had been invited to appear on 'This Evening'.

memories.memory_text: I told Mrs. Aubrey that I liked the attic very much, and she gave me a strange look before leaving, but I didn't understand why she was confused because this is what I call the place with the lanes and the balls.

memories.memory_text: I infer that An implied formal event for which Chance is preparing, where he will be publicly observed.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Chance responds to Eve's comment about watching with a simple affirmation of his own watching habits.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Eve enters Chance's room to wish him well before his appearance, conveying Benjamin's regards and expressing support.

memories.memory_text: I remember Eve stepping forward and impulsively kissing me on the cheek before she left.

memories.memory_text: I was told by the man who greeted me that he is Morton Hull, the producer of 'This Evening'.

memories.memory_text: I greeted the man who introduced himself as Morton Hull by saying, 'Hello, Morton.'

memories.memory_text: I remember Hull taking me into the television station after we were introduced.

memories.memory_text: I think I must be here for a scheduled appearance on 'This Evening', since Morton Hull introduced himself as its producer and then took me into the station.

memories.memory_text: Hull told me that my position in finance makes me ideally suited to explain the economic crisis to millions of viewers.

memories.memory_text: Hull mentioned that more people will watch me tonight than have seen theater plays in the last forty years, which I found hard to grasp.

memories.memory_text: I think there's going to be a big broadcast where I'll talk about the economic crisis, and a lot of people will be watching live, though I'm not entirely sure how it will go.

memories.memory_text: I was intrigued by the surroundings as Hull led me through the corridor and then took me into the make-up room.

memories.memory_text: I didn't see Constance go through my clothes and examine my shoe, but I noticed afterward that someone had been handling my things.

memories.memory_text: Colson gave me a glass of water and told me it was hot under the lights, and I told him I was very thirsty.

memories.memory_text: I watched the guest before me on the TV monitor, seeing William Dupont wrap up the segment on 'This Evening,' knowing I would be next.

memories.memory_text: I left the room, and I saw Colson pick up my water glass, wrap it in Kleenex, and put it in his pocket.

memories.memory_text: I made my first public appearance on television, introduced as a distinguished guest, walking onto the stage with a smile and a limp as the audience applauded and cameras followed me.

grounded_facts: Wilson informs Eve that he will take Chance to the third floor guest suite where Dr. Allenby is waiting.
memories.memory_text: I was waiting in the guest suite on the third floor when Wilson announced he would bring Chance to me.

grounded_facts: Eve confirms Wilson's plan to take Chance to the guest suite with Dr. Allenby present.
memories.memory_text: I knew Eve had approved Wilson's plan to bring Chance to the guest suite where I was waiting, since she confirmed it after he informed her.

grounded_facts: Dr. Allenby administers an injection to Chance's buttocks to ease pain and swelling from his injury.
A medical check-up conducted by Dr. Allenby on Chance following a leg injury, including injection, diagnosis, and care recommendations.
memories.memory_text: I administered an injection to Chance's buttocks after cleaning the area with alcohol, telling him it would ease the pain and swelling from his leg injury and that he'd barely feel it.

grounded_facts: Chance tells Allenby the injection hurt despite his reassurance that it wouldn't.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Chance that the injection hurt, even though I had assured him it wouldn't.

grounded_facts: Chance reveals that Thomas Franklin, an attorney, previously asked him about a claim, which alarms Allenby.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Thomas Franklin, an attorney, had asked Chance about a claim, which immediately made me uneasy.

grounded_facts: Allenby directly asks Chance if he plans to make a legal claim against the Rands, showing suspicion and concern.
Dr. Allenby directly asks Chance if he plans to make a legal claim against the Rands, and Chance denies any intention to do so.
memories.memory_text: I asked Chance directly if he was planning to make a legal claim against the Rands, and I felt my concern ease when he told me there was no need for one.

grounded_facts: Dr. Allenby recommends that Chance stay at the estate for a day or two and undergo X-rays, citing the availability of an on-site hospital due to Benjamin's illness.
memories.memory_text: I recommended that Mr. Gardiner stay at the estate for a day or two and have his leg X-rayed, since we have an on-site hospital available due to Benjamin's illness, and I wanted to ensure he received proper care.

grounded_facts: Allenby suggests that Mr. Gardiner stay at the mansion for a couple of days for observation after his injury.
memories.memory_text: I suggested that Mr. Gardiner stay at the mansion for a couple of days so I could keep an eye on him after his injury, since I didn't find any serious damage but wanted to be cautious.

grounded_facts: Allenby informs Eve that there has been no medical improvement in Ben's condition.
memories.memory_text: I told Eve there had been no medical improvement in Ben's condition, and I could see how much it hurt her to hear it.

grounded_facts: Eve shares her emotional struggle, expressing fleeting hope that Ben is improving despite the lack of medical improvement.
memories.memory_text: Eve told me she sometimes feels like Ben is getting stronger, that a look or movement gives her hope, even though I know there's been no real improvement.

grounded_facts: Eve and Allenby talk outside by the patio fireplace at night, discussing Gardiner's injury and Ben's condition.
memories.memory_text: I joined Eve by the patio fireplace at night, and we talked about Gardiner's injury and how Ben has been doing, though I could see she was struggling with her emotions.

grounded_facts: Allenby reaches out and holds Eve's hand after she expresses her emotional pain about Ben's condition.
memories.memory_text: I reached out and held Eve's hand after she shared how hard it was to accept what was happening to Ben.

grounded_facts: Chance discloses that his business was shut down and locked by attorneys after the death of 'the Old Man' and Louise leaving.
memories.memory_text: I heard Chance say that his business was shut down and locked by the attorneys after the Old Man died and Louise left.

grounded_facts: Eve expresses sympathy for Chance's losses and offers assistance with the estate's facilities.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve express sympathy for Chance's losses and offer access to the estate's facilities if needed, making sure Chance felt welcome and supported during a difficult time.

grounded_facts: Rand shifts from formal address to proposing a first-name basis, signaling growing rapport.
memories.memory_text: I saw Rand shift from formal address and invite Chance to call him Ben, which signaled a growing rapport between them.

grounded_facts: Allenby smiles and invites Chance to call him Robert, furthering social integration.
memories.memory_text: I smiled and invited Chance to call me Robert, wanting to make things more personal and help him feel included.

grounded_facts: Rand enthusiastically affirms Chance's identification as a gardener, elevating it to a metaphor for productive capitalism.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Rand enthusiastically affirm Chance's identity as a gardener, praising it as a metaphor for productive capitalism—he said a businessman is like a gardener who makes barren soil fruitful through hard work and creates value for family and community.

grounded_facts: A formal dinner gathering at Rand's estate with guests including Allenby, Eve, and Chance, where conversation turns to business, regulation, and personal circumstances.
memories.memory_text: I was at a formal dinner at Rand's estate where I gave Chance a look and later studied him as the conversation turned to business and personal matters.

grounded_facts: Rand probes Chance's knowledge of him, framing honesty as rare and valuable.
memories.memory_text: I heard Rand say to Chance that no man knows everything about another, but few are honest enough to admit it, framing honesty as rare and valuable while probing what Chance knew about him.

grounded_facts: Rand offers Chance a cigar from his humidor, initiating a gesture of camaraderie and testing.
memories.memory_text: I saw Rand offer Chance a cigar from his humidor and then hand him an ornate lighter after lighting his own, using the gesture to initiate camaraderie and test Chance.

grounded_facts: Rand reveals his intention to start a financial assistance program for struggling American businessmen, framing it as a defense of middle-class values.
memories.memory_text: I heard Rand say he was concerned about struggling American businessmen and that he wanted to start a financial assistance program to help them against inflation, excessive taxation, and other problems.

grounded_facts: Chance explicitly states he has no thoughts on the proposed financial program.
memories.memory_text: I heard Chance say 'No, Ben' when asked about the financial program, making it clear he didn't want to engage.

grounded_facts: Allenby declares it time for his patients to prepare for bed, asserting medical authority over both Chance and Rand.
memories.memory_text: I declared it time for my patients to prepare for bed, asserting my role as their doctor and ending the discussion.

grounded_facts: Rand positions businessmen as 'Gardeners' defending freedom against 'pollutants', attempting to align Chance with his worldview.
memories.memory_text: I saw Rand position businessmen as 'Gardeners' defending freedom against 'pollutants', and he tried to get Chauncey to align with that view, even mentioning me and kid lawyers as common foes.

grounded_facts: A nighttime meeting in Rand's pool room where Rand engages Chance in conversation about ideology and potential collaboration.
memories.memory_text: I opened the door and watched as Rand entered in his wheelchair, followed by Chance being pushed by Wilson; I observed Chance struggling to light the cigar while Rand spoke and eventually put it aside, and later I laughed as I took Rand's cigar and snuffed it out to end the meeting.

grounded_facts: Allenby physically removes Rand's cigar and ends the meeting, asserting control over Rand's behavior under medical pretense.
memories.memory_text: I took Rand's cigar and snuffed it out, using my medical authority to stop his behavior and close the meeting.

grounded_facts: Allenby reveals that the President will attend the Financial Institute meeting in place of Benjamin Rand.
memories.memory_text: I told Chance that the President offered to sit in for Benjamin at the meeting, which I thought was quite a nice gesture.

grounded_facts: Annual meeting of Benjamin Rand's Financial Institute, from which he is excused due to health.
memories.memory_text: I was aware that Benjamin Rand was supposed to speak at the annual meeting of his Financial Institute, but I excused him due to his health, and I learned the President would step in for him, which I thought was a kind gesture.

grounded_facts: Chance becomes aware that he is expected to meet the President at ten o'clock, gaining time-sensitive knowledge.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Ben that Chance is expected to meet the President at ten o'clock in his room, so I confirmed the timing with Chance to ensure he was aware.

grounded_facts: Chance reveals he already knows about the President's visit, surprising Allenby.
memories.memory_text: I was surprised when Chance told me he already knew about the President's visit—he said Ben had called him and asked him to meet at ten o'clock.

grounded_facts: Chance is scheduled to meet the President in Benjamin Rand's room at ten o'clock.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Chance was scheduled to meet the President in Benjamin Rand's room at ten o'clock, a detail he confirmed after mentioning that Ben had called and instructed him directly.

grounded_facts: Chance chooses to walk instead of using the wheelchair, indicating improved mobility and desire for independence.
memories.memory_text: I saw Chance decide to walk instead of using the wheelchair, telling Wilson he wanted to walk to meet the President.

grounded_facts: Allenby examines Chance's injured leg, assessing recovery progress.
memories.memory_text: I examined Chance's injured leg outside the mansion and noticed the swelling had gone down considerably; I asked him if he felt pain in certain spots, and he told me yes but that it wasn't bad, which I took as a positive sign of recovery.

grounded_facts: Allenby decides to go to Chance's room after stepping off the elevator and pausing briefly in thought.
memories.memory_text: I decided to go to Chance's room after stepping off the elevator and taking a moment to think.

grounded_facts: Allenby is looking through Chancel's clothes for identification.
memories.memory_text: I was searching through Chancel's clothes to find some sort of identification.

grounded_facts: Riff enters the room and introduces himself as being from the Secret Service.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riff enter the room and look around, interrupting what I was doing.

grounded_facts: Riff tells Allenby his name and affiliation with the Secret Service.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Riff that his name is Riff and he's with the Secret Service.

grounded_facts: Riff uses a metal detector to scan Allenby's clothing.
Riff performs a security scan on Allenby using a metal detector.
memories.memory_text: I was scanned by Riff with a metal detector as part of a security check while Perkins watched.

grounded_facts: A group gathers in Rand's bedroom to watch the President's televised address to the Financial Institute.
memories.memory_text: I was in Rand's bedroom with Eve, Chance, and the nurses, watching the President's address on TV together.

grounded_facts: The President cites Rand and Chance in his address, quoting Chance's gardening metaphor as economic insight.

grounded_facts: After Rand's death, Allenby probes Chance's relationship with Eve and confirms his identity as a gardener.
memories.memory_text: I observed Chance after Rand's passing and questioned how close he truly was to Eve; I asked him directly if he was really just a gardener, needing to confirm his role.

grounded_facts: Chance declares his intention to tell Eve about Rand's death.
memories.memory_text: Chance smiled at me and said, 'I'll go tell Eve about Ben now, Robert,' making it clear he intends to inform her about Rand's death.

grounded_facts: Chance departs from the funeral service abruptly while the President is speaking, walking into the surrounding trees.
memories.memory_text: I saw Chance abruptly leave the funeral service while the President was still speaking, walking into the trees around the mausoleum.

grounded_facts: A formal funeral gathering held at the Rand family mausoleum, attended by mourners including the President of the United States, who delivers a eulogy for Benjamin Rand.
memories.memory_text: I was present at the formal funeral gathering for Benjamin Rand at the family mausoleum, where the President delivered a eulogy.

grounded_facts: The President reads personal quotes from Benjamin Rand during the eulogy, revealing Rand's self-awareness, humor, and philosophical reflections.
memories.memory_text: I listened as the President read Benjamin Rand's words during the eulogy, and I could hear Rand's self-awareness and wit in quotes like when he said, 'When I was a boy, I was told that the Lord fashioned us from his own image. That's when I decided to manufacture mirrors.'

grounded_facts: The funeral service for Rand concludes, marking the end of the formal ceremony.
The funeral of Rand, a formal outdoor ceremony attended by key figures including the President and First Lady.
memories.memory_text: I was present when the formal outdoor funeral service for Rand ended, and I saw that it was attended by key figures including the President and the First Lady.

grounded_facts: Eve expresses appreciation to the President for the funeral service.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve thank the President, calling him 'Bobby' and saying the service was very moving.

grounded_facts: President conveys sympathy to Eve over Rand's death.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the President express his sympathy to Eve, saying, 'We're all going to miss him.'

grounded_facts: The President notices Mr. Gardiner is missing and inquires about his whereabouts.
memories.memory_text: I was present when the President noticed Mr. Gardiner was missing and asked about his whereabouts.

grounded_facts: Chauncey Gardiner departs from the funeral grounds, overwhelmed by emotion.
memories.memory_text: I saw Chauncey Gardiner walk off from the funeral grounds because he was overwhelmed by emotion.

grounded_facts: First Lady expresses sorrow for Eve's loss and promises to call.
memories.memory_text: I saw the First Lady offer her sorrow to Eve, saying she was sorry for her loss, and then promise to call her soon.

grounded_facts: A funeral gathering for Rand, attended by mourners including Eve and Allenby, taking place outdoors during the day.
memories.memory_text: I attended Rand's funeral outdoors during the day, and after most mourners left, I walked with Eve toward the limousine, glancing around for Chance.

grounded_facts: Eve questions whether they should look for Chance and expresses her wish for his presence at the funeral.
memories.memory_text: Eve asked me if we should look for Chance, and she said she wished he were here, which I remember hearing as we walked.

grounded_facts: A funeral gathering for Rand, taking place outdoors during the day, attended by Jeffrey, Eve, and Allenby.
Jeffrey holds the car door open for Eve and Allenby, providing physical assistance as they enter the car.
Eve displays visible concern before getting into the car after the funeral.
memories.memory_text: I attended Rand's funeral outdoors during the day, and as Eve and I prepared to leave, I saw her looking worried before getting into the car; Jeffrey held the door open for both of us, helping us as we got in.

grounded_facts: Eve urgently appeals to Allenby, expressing deep concern for Chance and urging immediate action to find him.
memories.memory_text: I remember Eve urgently telling me we had to find Chance because he could be lost or in danger, and she insisted we couldn't leave him.

grounded_facts: Allenby acknowledges Eve's emotional attachment to Chance, noting her genuine care.
memories.memory_text: I noticed how much Eve cares for Chance and I asked her directly if she really felt that way about him.

grounded_facts: Robert Allenby decides to search for Chance after Eve expresses concern and urges action.
memories.memory_text: After hearing Eve's plea and seeing how much she cared, I decided we should go look for Chance and I said so out loud.

grounded_facts: Jeffrey calls out to draw attention to Chance crossing the road.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jeffrey call out sharply, saying 'Look!' to get our attention.

grounded_facts: Chance is seen crossing the road ahead, prompting the group to stop and take notice.
memories.memory_text: I saw Chance crossing the road about 100 yards ahead and continuing down a hill, which made us stop and take notice.

grounded_facts: Eve exclaims upon seeing Chance, confirming his identity.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve exclaim, 'There he is! Chauncey!', confirming that the figure was Chance.

grounded_facts: David stops the vehicle at the spot where Chance crossed, enabling pursuit.
memories.memory_text: I saw David stop the limousine at the spot where Chance had crossed.

grounded_facts: Eve quickly leaves the vehicle after spotting Chance, initiating direct pursuit.
memories.memory_text: I watched Eve quickly leave the vehicle right after she spotted Chance, starting her pursuit.

grounded_facts: Chance and Eve reunite after a period of separation, with emotional embrace and mutual expressions of concern.
Eve calls out to Chance and expresses relief and affection upon finding him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve call out to Chance and rush down the hill to embrace him tightly, clearly relieved and emotional after they found him separated from us.

grounded_facts: Allenby greets Chance with a handshake and an arm around the shoulder upon his return.
memories.memory_text: I greeted Chance with a handshake and put my arm around his shoulder when he returned.

grounded_facts: Eve leads Chance back up the hill to the waiting limousine, where Allenby greets him and they all enter the vehicle.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve lead Chance back up the hill to the limousine, and then I greeted him before we all got into the vehicle together.

grounded_facts: A reunion event occurring beside a waiting limousine after Chance is found separated from the group.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the reunion beside the waiting limousine, where Eve led Chance back up the hill and then the three of us got in together.

memories.memory_text: I proposed the idea of a financial assistance program for struggling businessmen while shooting pool, framing them as 'Gardeners' who need protection from the 'pollutants' undermining our economy—Chance didn't respond at first, but I could see he was listening, even if he was distracted by not knowing how to light his cigar.

I remember telling Chauncey that no one likes a dying man because people fear death, but that he was different—his calm, balanced presence didn't waver between fear and hope, and I truly admired that in him.

I remember telling Chance about my past thoughts of public office, how influence could be wielded quietly, and then suggesting—almost like a passing of the torch—that he might one day stand where I stood, in a position of eminence, needing to stay honest and open.
I introduced Chauncey to the President, calling him my dear friend—my voice was weak, but I made sure the words carried weight as I sat down, needing the chair more than I wanted to show.

I told the President the truth — that inflation, taxation, and foreign energy dependence have pushed the Free Enterprise System to its breaking point, and we’re on the brink of a crash from which we might not recover.

I leaned on Chance as we walked down the hall, my arm around him, feeling how steady he was—even as my own strength gave out. I told him I wanted him to lead the financial program, that he was the right man, and asked him to meet with the Board, though I could see he didn’t remember our talk from the night before.
I asked Chauncey to go to Sophie Rowley’s reception in my place and escort Eve—he said yes, and I could already imagine the two of them causing a stir among the guests.
I reached out and held Chauncey’s hand, thanking him—really thanking him—and when I let go, I told Robert I was ready, knowing Eve and Chauncey would leave me soon after.

I told them 'everything'—and meant it—though Monroe hesitated, as if the word weren't precise enough for ledgers and law; but love isn't measured in holdings, and Eve has given me more than any balance sheet could hold.
I told Robert no more needles—I can feel the end coming, but I don’t fear it, not with Chauncey here to take care of things.
I stopped Teresa from swabbing my arm and asked her to bring me Chauncey Gardiner—he’s the one who’ll head it up now.
I reached for Chauncey’s hand, needing to feel its strength one last time, and asked him to stay with Eve—she’s a delicate flower, and she needs him.
I wish he were here... I kept looking, hoping to see him, but the space beside me stayed empty.

I proposed a financial assistance program for struggling businessmen while shooting pool, called them 'Gardeners' defending the country's values, and asked Chance for his thoughts. He said no at first, then said he could give it some thought but mentioned his sore leg.

I told Chauncey that real influence doesn't require public office—that wealth and position bring responsibility, not just power, and that he might one day stand where I have stood, if he remains grounded.

I stopped to confirm the Caracas agreement papers had arrived, and when Mrs. Aubrey said they were ready for my signature, I felt a quiet satisfaction—this was one more duty I could still carry out, despite the weight in my bones.
I introduced Chauncey to the President as my dear friend, leaning on the chair to steady myself, and saw the President smile despite the odd thing Chauncey said about his height on television.

I told the President the truth about the economy—that inflation, taxation, foreign energy dependence, and the free enterprise system had all reached their breaking point, and that we were on the brink of a crash from which we might not recover.

I leaned on Chance as we walked down the hall, my arm around him, feeling the effort it took just to stay upright—yet I knew I had to make him understand he was the one I wanted to lead the financial assistance program, the one to carry it forward.
I heard the President mention my name and Chance's on television, and for a moment, I felt a flicker of pride—like the flame before it goes out—before the coughing took hold again.
I asked Chance to go to Sophie Rowley's reception in my place and escort Eve, knowing I couldn't go myself—Robert wouldn't allow it, and my body won't permit much anymore.
I reached out and held Chance's hand—felt the strength in it—and thanked him, knowing he'd carry forward what I can no longer do.
I lie in bed, unable to move much, my body failing me, but my mind still turning over the weight of what comes next.
I told them 'everything'—Monroe wanted precision, but what’s more precise than leaving every last thing to Eve? I may be weak, but I’m still in love, and that’s the clearest truth I know.
I told Robert no more needles—I can feel the end coming, but I don’t fear it. Knowing Chauncey is here, that he’ll take care of things, makes it easier.
I stopped Teresa from swabbing my arm—I didn’t want the transfusion. I asked her to get Mr. Gardiner instead, because he’s the one who’ll head things up now.
I reached for Chauncey’s hand, needing to feel its strength one last time, and asked him to stay with Eve—she’s a delicate flower, and she needs him.
I told Chauncey I was fond of him, that my associates wanted to meet him, and that he should tell Eve I’m madly in love with her—then I let go.
I remember Eve’s voice, soft and aching, saying she wished I were there—standing by my own grave, unseen, as they walked away.

relations.relation_summary: Ben Rand and the President share a close, respectful, and emotionally supportive relationship characterized by mutual admiration and professional trust. Social relationship evidence reveals that Rand serves as an adviser and confidant to the President, offering guidance on sensitive matters such as the risks of delivering a straightforward speech. The President values Rand's input, thanking him for his 'time and thoughts' and acknowledging his role as a trusted associate. This professional dynamic is deepened by personal affection: the President refers to Rand as 'Ben,' 'my friend,' and 'goodfriend,' and engages in intimate physical gestures such as clasping his hand and guiding him to a chair, signaling warmth and concern. Rand reciprocates this respect, describing the President as 'a decent fellow' and expressing sympathy for the burdens of his position. Their shared events—discussing the speech's risks, exchanging insights on governance, and engaging in personal dialogue—reinforce both the emotional and functional dimensions of their bond. These interactions suggest a relationship that blends formal advisory duties with genuine friendship, influencing the President’s decision-making through trusted counsel and emotional reassurance. The relationship appears stable and consistent across the evidence, with no indication of conflict or evolution, but rather a sustained connection built on cooperation, respect, and personal regard.

Ben Rand and Eve are married, and their relationship is characterized by deep emotional and physical affection, consistent with a romantic and intimate bond. Social relationship evidence highlights multiple instances of mutual care and tenderness: Rand refers to Eve as a 'delicate flower' and entrusts Chance with her protection, indicating a protective and nurturing attitude. Eve reciprocates with physical affection—kissing Rand and holding his hand—and expresses emotional concern for his health, particularly during moments when he appears fatigued. Rand, in turn, displays affection by squeezing Eve's hand and kissing it, reinforcing their role as affectionate partners. Their shared events further illustrate their closeness: they are repeatedly shown together watching the President's address on television, physically close and emotionally synchronized, such as when they squeeze hands during a moment of excitement involving Chance's appearance. They also engage in intimate dialogue about Rand's declining health, revealing vulnerability and emotional interdependence. These interactions suggest that their relationship is not only romantic but also rooted in companionship and mutual support during times of personal and societal change. The evidence indicates a stable, loving marriage marked by tenderness and concern, with no indication of conflict or evolution beyond deepening emotional solidarity in the face of illness and external events. The relationship influences Rand's openness to Chance, as his care for Eve motivates him to ensure her continued well-being through others.

The relationship between Ben Rand and Chance is characterized by deep mutual respect, emotional support, and a strong sense of trust that evolves into a meaningful mentor-mentee dynamic. Rand consistently expresses admiration for Chance’s simplicity, naturalness, and perceived philosophical depth, referring to him as his 'most insightful friend' and 'my dear friend'—labels he uses in high-stakes social contexts, such as when introducing Chance to the President. This indicates not only personal affection but also public validation of their bond. Rand demonstrates paternal affection by calling Chance 'my boy' and encouraging him with motivational language, urging him not to surrender and referencing shared experiences like 'the Room Upstairs,' which suggests emotional investment in Chance’s well-being and growth. The social evidence reveals a relationship built on trust: Rand entrusts Chance with the care of Eve and assigns him leadership of the Financial Assistance Program, showing confidence in his judgment and character. Chance, in turn, responds with cooperation and loyalty, agreeing to help and remaining a steady presence. Their interactions are marked by politeness, camaraderie, and symbolic gestures—such as cigar offerings and shared meals—reinforcing a host-guest relationship that deepens into genuine friendship. Joint events further illustrate their closeness: they are frequently seen together in intimate settings—discussing life in the library, watching the President’s address side by side, sharing meals, and physically supporting each other during movement. Rand’s physical reliance on Chance, and his act of putting an arm around him for support, symbolize both literal and metaphorical interdependence. The repeated scenes of watching television together and engaging in dialogue underscore their shared narrative space and emotional alignment. Rand’s laughter at Chance’s remarks and his 'Bravo!' in response to Chance’s gardening metaphors reveal that he not only respects but is emotionally moved by Chance’s words, interpreting them as profound insights. This dynamic transforms Chance from a mere house guest into a trusted confidant and symbolic heir. The relationship evolves from a hospitable arrangement into a cooperative alliance, especially as Rand identifies shared adversaries (lawyers and physicians), framing their bond as one of solidarity against external forces. Overall, the emotional dynamic is one of warmth, reverence, and protective guidance from Rand, met with quiet loyalty and sincerity from Chance, profoundly influencing Rand’s decisions and public actions in Chance’s favor.

memories.memory_text: I saw the snow falling in the garden on the television and told Louise it was very white; when she said the Old Man had died, I remembered seeing such things happen before and said so, then decided it was time to work in the garden.
I remember saying 'I live here' to Thomas, feeling calm even as he looked at me with doubt, and then turning the question to the weather because it was cold outside and that was true.
I have never been in an automobile, not really—I only said that to answer Thomas, though I did sit in it from time to time, just inside here.
I told them, 'I live in here,' and then I turned toward my room, knowing they would follow.

I showed Thomas and Sally the television the Old Man gave me, and how it has remote control—just like his. I also told them I take the Old Man’s suits from the attic; they all fit me well, and I’ve seen on television that the style is back.
Franklin asked me to sign a paper. I said I don't know how. I told him I have no claim and am fine. He said I must leave the house.

I asked the men on the corner if they knew where I could find a garden to work in, and one of them asked what I was growing, but I didn't get to answer before the leader came close and started shouting.
I took out my remote and clicked it three times at the man, but it didn't work, so I put it back in my pocket when he pulled out a knife.
I saw myself on the television screen in the store window—when I moved my arm, the image moved too, and I smiled to make sure it was really me.
I was standing between the cars, trying to get back on the screen, when the large car behind me moved and pushed me against the other one—I felt pain and dropped my suitcase and changer.

I remember sitting in the soft seat of the large car, feeling the soreness in my leg, and saying yes when Eve offered me a drink and to see her family doctor, though I didn’t understand what it meant.
I turned on the TV after the doctor finished with the injection, because the screen had been dark for too long.
I tried to light the cigar like the man on television, but it wouldn't catch, so I put it in the ashtray and smiled at Robert.
I told Eve that Ben reminds me of the Old Man, and she seemed surprised, but I meant it—Ben feels familiar, like someone I once knew in the garden.
I stood before the tapestry, then told Smythe I would like to go to Rand Memorial Hospital—to see Ben.
Ben talked about being in a position of eminence and how power could be blinding, and said I might one day be in such a position—I changed the channel and said 'I see, Ben.'
I felt Rand's arm around me, leaning his weight on my shoulder as we began to walk—he was unsteady, and I adjusted my pace to match his, feeling the pressure of his grip through my coat.
He called me 'Chauncey'—a name I didn’t recognize at first, spoken softly but with warmth, and I said yes, Ben, that’s a good idea, because it was clear he trusted me to be beside him.
I said 'You look much taller on television, Mr. President,' and he paused, then laughed, but I could feel Rand's quiet approval beside me.
I said, 'As long as the roots are not severed, all is well and all will be well in the garden,' and then explained how growth has its seasons—spring, summer, fall, winter—and how they return again.
The President smiled at me, said my sense was refreshing, and shook my hand before leaving—he seemed to admire something in what I said, though I was mostly noticing the books in the room.
Ben held my arm tightly as we walked, and he said I might be the man to lead the financial assistance program—he wants me to meet with the Board. I told him I understand.
I picked up the phone at the desk while the television sets played in the background, and I said hello.
Mrs. Aubrey found me in the bowling alley and said Morton Hull called. He wanted me to appear on 'This Evening' because the Vice President canceled. I said yes, I would like to be on that show.

I told the man I can't write and I can't read, and he smiled as if I had said something wise, then kept talking about a book with a ghostwriter and an advance, though I didn't understand what he meant by 'bed of roses' or why he laughed when I asked what kind of bed it was.
Ben asked me to stay with Eve, to take care of her like a delicate flower, and I told him I would—I remember holding his hand and feeling how weak it was.
After Ben died, Allenby questioned me about my relationship with Eve and whether I was really a gardener—I told him I love Eve and that I am a gardener, which made me smile.

I saw the snow falling in the garden on the television, and Louise came in upset, saying the Old Man was dead, but I had seen such things before on TV and knew it was something that happens to old people.
I agreed to let Eve Rand’s family doctor examine my leg because it was still sore, and going to her home seemed like a quiet, sensible solution.
When Eve asked for my name, I told her 'My name is Chance,' and when she thought I was someone else, I said, 'No. I'm a gardener,' to make it clear who I am.
I told Ben I was a very good gardener, and that everything in the garden I left had grown by the labor of my own hands, but now all I have is the room upstairs.
I said, 'As long as the roots are not severed, all is well and all will be well in the garden,' and then explained how growth has its seasons—spring, summer, fall, winter—and how they return again.
The President said the visit was enlightening, shook my hand, and I said, 'Yes. It has,' because it was nice, and I remember standing there looking at the books before I stood up to shake his hand.

memories.memory_text: I remember deciding to take Chance home instead of the hospital—after seeing how sore his leg still was, I thought our family doctor could help without all the fuss and impersonal waiting.

I offered him cognac and introduced myself, but when he coughed from the drink and kept searching his pockets for a remote control, I felt unsure how to reach him—still, I asked if he needed help and tried to keep the silence from growing too heavy.
I held Ben's hand against my cheek and asked if he'd heard about what happened, feeling the weight of the day settle over me when he confirmed he knew.

When Ben insisted I invite Mr. Gardiner to dinner and kissed my hand, I felt both touched and unsettled—his strength in that moment made it impossible to refuse, even though I wasn't sure it was wise.

I turned to Chauncey and asked if his injury would keep him from his work, then offered to contact someone for him—his quiet answer about the Old Man dying and Louise leaving hung in the air, and I could only say I was sorry.
I reached for Chauncey’s hand and told him how grateful I was that he was here… with us. My voice trembled, and I could feel the weight of everything in that moment.
I thought he was hesitating because he was worried about me, so I touched his shoulder and told him I’d be all right—that he should go. After he left, I said to Allenby how sensitive Chauncey is.
I remember saying 'Yes, I am, Ben'—my voice was soft, but I meant it more than I’ve said anything in a long time. When he took my hand, I felt it—the weight of being seen, and I didn’t look away.

I remember sitting on the edge of Ben's bed, feeling his eyes on me as he asked Chance to escort me to the reception—my face grew warm when he said we'd create a stir, as if I were someone worth noticing.
I saw Ben reach out his hand to Chance, and Chance held it. Ben said thank you, then let go. After that, Chance and I left the room quietly.
I stopped by my bedroom door and told Chauncey I didn’t have many friends, that Benjamin’s friends were all much older—I said it softly, almost like I was afraid to admit it.
I looked at him for a long moment, then kissed him on the lips—I remember the quiet, how I stepped back and smiled before saying good night, like I was trying to keep it light.
I told Chauncey I loved him, then began to cry—first quietly, then more—while he kept watching TV.

After I calmed down, I told him I was grateful—because even though I would have given myself to him completely, he didn’t take it, and that made me feel safe, even if he seemed confused by what I meant.
I introduced Chauncey to Mr. Watson at the reception, and they shook hands. Chauncey said it was a pleasure.
Sophie embraced me first, then hugged Chauncey tightly—she was so eager to meet him, and I remember feeling a little overwhelmed by how quickly she pulled us both into the crowd.
I remember saying Benjamin was doing as well as could be expected, and that he still spoke of his talks with the Ambassador—then excusing myself when Sophie pulled me away to let the men talk.
I remember standing there, hearing Rand tell the attorneys to give me everything—his voice was weak but so certain, and I could feel the weight of what he was doing, even if I didn’t speak.
He said he was still in love, and that he had endless faith in me—those words hung in the air, so tender and raw, and I don’t know if I’ve ever felt so deeply seen and trusted.
I held Chauncey’s hand and told him how safe I felt with him, how close—my voice trembled a little, but I needed him to know that Benjamin understands my feelings for him.
I opened my bedroom door and asked him to come in—then closed it behind us, my heart pounding, the air suddenly quieter, just the two of us inside.
I kissed him, held him close, ran my hands over his body, but he didn’t respond—just kept watching the TV like I wasn’t even there.
He said he 'likes to watch'—and when I touched myself under the covers, he changed the channel and yawned as I came… then just said 'Good night' and left.

I stood beside Chance as the President spoke, and then he just turned and walked away into the trees without a word — I remember the cold air, the snow underfoot, and how I stayed still, watching him go.
I said Chauncey was sensitive and overcome with grief when the President asked where he was.
I kept looking around, hoping to see Chance, wishing he were there with us—his absence felt heavy as we walked to the limousine.
I ran down the hill toward Chauncey, my voice breaking as I called his name, and when I reached him, I held him so tightly—I was trembling, overwhelmed with relief that he was safe.
I invited Chance to come home with us so Dr. Allenby could look at his leg—hospitals are so impersonal, and it felt like the right thing to do, even with a stranger in the car.
I offered Chance cognac and introduced myself, but he coughed when he drank it—then he kept searching his pockets for a remote control, which confused me a little.

I handed my coat to Greta and told Wilson I’d be with Mr. Rand if needed, then said to Chance I’d see him after the doctor checked his leg—he looked around the hallway like he wasn’t sure where he was.
I held Ben's hand against my cheek and told him Mr. Gardiner was reasonable, but when he joked about meeting him for dinner, I couldn't answer—there was just silence between us.
I asked Robert how Mr. Gardiner was. When he suggested Chance stay, I questioned if it was necessary. I said Chance was different, not like people we usually meet in Washington.

I put my tea down and asked Robert if there had been any improvement in Ben, and when he said no, I just went quiet—staring into the dark, holding onto moments where Ben seemed almost like himself again, even though I know it's not real.

I asked Chauncey about the old man he mentioned, and when he said he was very close to him, I could hear the quiet sadness in his voice—he didn’t say much, but I understood how much he must have meant to him.

When I asked about Louise and he said she was just the maid who brought him meals, I felt a sudden relief—I had worried there might have been someone else, someone from his past I didn’t know about, but then that weight lifted.
I told Chauncey that Benjamin and I would be watching him on TV tonight—he seemed pleased by that.
I stepped forward and kissed Chauncey on the cheek—I wasn't planning to, but it felt right in the moment—and then I left, a little flustered.
I told Chauncey I loved him and wanted us to be very close—so close—and for a moment, I let myself believe he might feel the same.
I started to cry after I kissed him and he didn’t kiss me back—his arm around me felt like comfort, not love, and I realized my feelings weren’t returned.
